A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Unisolver, and their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison. Retained material can be matched across the substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark evaluations, ablations, generalization experiments and scaling analyses for Unisolver.

after.justification: V3 retains original experimental results and adds baseline comparisons, missing-component experiments, embedding analyses and equation-transfer results.

M1.justification: The core embeddings, decoupled conditioning and Transformer architecture remain intact. V3 adds an adaptation for incomplete PDE information: replacing components with learnable tokens at 30% probability and permitting inference with missing components (Section 4.4).

E1.justification: The three benchmark collections and represented PDE families remain. V3 adds partially observed HeterNS evaluation, changing the available input information (Figure 7). The equation-order transfer experiment repartitions the existing 1D family rather than adding a new dataset or domain.

E2.justification: HeterNS comparisons expand from FNO, Factformer and ViT to also include PINO, ICON and MPP, including the double-unseen comparison (v1 Table 12; v3 Table 13). This substantially broadens comparator types. PDEformer-L and DPOT-S remain, despite shortened names in v3.

E3.justification: V1 describes 1D evaluation using two 10,000-sample subsets selected from pretraining data; v3 describes 10,000 generated in-distribution test samples. Factformer's reported size changes from 9.4M to 5.1M despite unchanged listed architecture settings. New protocols include component masking and equation-order transfer with 200-epoch fine-tuning versus 500-epoch scratch training. These are reported setting changes, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V3 adds a random-vector control for symbolic embeddings, PCA analyses, HeterNS component ablations, missing-information robustness, equation-order transfer and full-trajectory case studies. Conversely, v1's subspace-ratio sensitivity study and separate 1D Concat-D/Concat-P analysis are removed or replaced (v1 Appendix E.2–E.3; v3 Section 4.4 and Appendix G).

E5.justification: V1 provides no repeated-run counts or uncertainty estimates. V3 Appendix G.5 reports three repetitions and introduces HeterNS standard deviations and 99% confidence labels in Tables 18–19. This establishes new uncertainty reporting, not an increase from a known earlier run count; the confidence calculation and baseline variability are insufficiently specified.

E6.justification: V3 adds extensive baseline and analysis results. Table 16, for example, reports 0.1624 after fine-tuning versus 0.3308 from scratch with 5,000 target examples under different training budgets. Factformer's Table 3 error at viscosity 1e-5 and force coefficient 2 changes from 0.0438 to 0.0571 alongside its changed reported size. Most primary Unisolver scores remain; fine-tuning evidence moves to Appendix A rather than disappearing.

T1.justification: The vibrating-string solution, two supporting lemmas and odd-periodic-extension proof are retained (v1 Appendix B; v3 Appendix D). Renumbering, notation edits and the standard relative-drop reporting formula do not substantively change the theoretical analysis.

C1.justification: The main contributions—complete PDE conditioning, decoupled Transformer subspaces and strong generalization—remain. However, the introduction replaces v1's assertion that correct prediction without complete PDE information is theoretically impossible with a qualified account allowing implicit information extraction while emphasizing its difficulty.

C2.justification: V3 adds interpretations connecting embedding geometry to PDE complexity and coefficient variation, and broadens applicability discussion to missing components and equivalent symbolic representations. Similar performance across LLMs is now attributed to sufficient mathematical knowledge, replacing v1's tentative explanation involving limited ablation data and prompts. The periodic-boundary Concat-P qualification is removed; the grid-data limitation remains.

D1.justification: V3 substantially expands reproducibility information: ICON's five prompting trajectories, PINO's 0.1 physics-loss weight, checkpoint selection, INR decoder depths, dataset sample counts and interpolation, 576 symbolic formulations with prompt examples, and the 32-A100 hardware configuration. It also changes the HeterNS access link. Many additions disclose existing implementation details rather than establish procedural changes.

R1.justification: V3 adds ICON to the generalizable-solver discussion and Poseidon to the limitations comparison, alongside supporting references on PCA, mathematical background and physics-informed learning. Some references, including the explicit T5 and LLaMA-2 entries, disappear although those models remain evaluated. The overall research positioning remains recognizable.

P1.justification: Substantial paragraph rewriting spans the introduction, method explanations, experiments and benchmark descriptions. V3 standardizes the narrative around joint training, in-distribution testing and zero-shot generalization, moves fine-tuning discussion into a dedicated appendix, and reorganizes supplementary material extensively.

P2.justification: V3 expands Table 1 with inputs and examples, groups HeterNS columns by evaluation setting, and converts fine-tuning table entries into appendix bar charts. It adds benchmark illustrations, PCA plots, robustness charts, trajectory displays and uncertainty tables, while also changing the document typography and layout.

improvement.justification: V3 substantially strengthens v1's generalization evidence through broader HeterNS comparators and targeted missing-component and unseen-equation tests. Expanded implementation details and run-variability reporting improve assessability. These gains outweigh the removed ratio-sensitivity study and reporting weaknesses, including underexplained 99% confidence labels and the retained 41.3% double-unseen summary, which disagrees with the revised Table 13 average of about 38.5%.
